name: Challenge the Status Quo
definition: Question the way things are done and look for the unconventional answer. Nothing is settled simply because it is established.

rows.situation: When the answer is that this is how it is done here
rows.under: Accepts it. The reason was lost years ago and nobody checks.
rows.justRight: Asks what it was for. If the reason is gone, changes it.
rows.over: Changes things that were working, and the team spends the quarter recovering.

rows.situation: When the thing to challenge is yours
rows.under: Defends it because you built it.
rows.justRight: Holds your own work to the same question, and unwinds it when the answer says so.
rows.over: Rebuilds your own decisions so often that nothing is allowed to settle.

rows.situation: When the standard solution would work
rows.under: Takes it without checking whether it fits.
rows.justRight: Takes it if it fits, and says explicitly why the unconventional option was rejected.
rows.over: Rejects the standard answer for being standard, and pays to rediscover it.

rows.situation: When the thing that makes no sense came from above
rows.under: Assumes there is a reason you are not senior enough to see.
rows.justRight: Asks for the reason. If there is none, says so.
rows.over: Treats every decision from above as suspect, and stops being useful in the room.

rows.situation: When the constraint is a real rule
rows.under: Treats every rule as immovable, including the internal ones nobody owns.
rows.justRight: Separates the rules that come from the regulator from the ones the company invented, and challenges the second kind.
rows.over: Challenges a real compliance boundary and puts the license at risk.
